clue.text: Inner cities had become disorderly, getting cut off

indicators.note: the letters before this phrase have been thrown into disorder, so they are rearranged

parts.note: fodder taken as written; 'had' does double duty in the surface but is part of the letters

explanation.surface: A grim report on urban decline: the inner cities fell into disorder and were left isolated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'had' looks like part of the indicator phrase, but its letters are needed: INNER CITIES HAD has the fourteen letters required.
explanation.definitionFit: Disinheritance is the act of being cut off from an inheritance, as when a parent cuts off a child in a will.

clue.text: Femme fatale lied disgracefully and upset prince

indicators.note: behaving disgracefully suggests the letters of 'lied' have gone astray and are rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: Prince Hal, the young Henry V in Shakespeare

explanation.surface: A seductress tells shameful lies and causes trouble for a prince.
explanation.walkthrough: DELI is the anagram of LIED; HAL (Shakespeare's Prince Hal) turned up gives LAH.
explanation.definitionFit: Delilah, who betrayed Samson by having his hair cut, is the Biblical archetype of the treacherous seductress.

clue.text: Prominent figure in New York moved there from France

definitions.text: Prominent figure in New York moved there from France

parts.words: Prominent figure in New York moved there from France
parts.note: reads like a celebrity who emigrated, but the figure is a literal one: a famous statue given by France and shipped across the Atlantic

explanation.walkthrough: 'Figure' suggests a well-known person; it is a sculpted figure. The statue was a gift from France, built there and shipped to New York in pieces in 1885.
explanation.definitionFit: The colossal copper statue in New York Harbor was designed by Bartholdi in Paris and sent over as a French gift.

clue.text: A swan, deprived of space, sits on this river

definitions.text: A swan, deprived of space, sits on this river

parts.words: A swan, deprived of space, sits on this river
parts.note: close up the space between 'A' and 'swan' and you get the name of an Egyptian city and dam, which stands on the river wanted

explanation.walkthrough: The swan is a red herring: remove the space from 'A swan' to get ASWAN, the Egyptian city famous for its High Dam, which lies on the NILE.
explanation.definitionFit: Aswan stands on the east bank of the great African river, at the First Cataract in southern Egypt.

clue.text: Catch colleague, endlessly shown up

indicators.note: in a down clue, shown up means written upwards, so the letters read backwards
without its end, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a partner is a colleague or associate

explanation.surface: Someone catches out a workmate, who is shown up for good measure.
explanation.walkthrough: PARTNER loses its last letter to give PARTNE, which read upwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrap someone is to catch them by trickery, luring them into a snare.

clue.text: Shut up about a Tory leader being inexperienced

indicators.note: the first word goes around the next pieces, as if about them

parts.note: to immure is to shut up within walls

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter T

explanation.surface: A political jibe: lock up the Tory leader, who is too green for the job.
explanation.walkthrough: IMMURE goes about A and T (the Tory leader).
explanation.definitionFit: Someone immature is not yet fully grown or developed, lacking the experience of an adult.

clue.text: Charge about, protecting us in battle

indicators.note: the pieces go inside the word for battle

parts.note: an action is a battle or fight

indicators.note: to protect is to surround, so the abbreviation for about goes around 'us'

parts.note: CA is circa, about

explanation.surface: A military order: charge around, shielding us in the fight.
explanation.walkthrough: CA is circa, Latin for about; 'Charge' looks like a cavalry order but is the noun meaning an allegation.
explanation.definitionFit: An accusation is a charge laid against someone, a formal claim of wrongdoing.

clue.text: Take irrevocable step in crucial problem, dividing religious objects

indicators.note: the phrase splits the two religious objects, sitting between them

parts.note: a cross and an icon, two objects of devotion
'the rub' is the crucial difficulty, as in Hamlet's 'there's the rub'

explanation.surface: Someone takes a decisive step over a thorny problem that splits believers over their sacred objects.
explanation.walkthrough: THE RUB, from Hamlet's 'Ay, there's the rub', divides CROSS from ICON.
explanation.definitionFit: Julius Caesar's crossing of the river Rubicon in 49 BC committed him to civil war, so the idiom means passing a point of no return.

clue.text: Basic accommodation in county, just what's needed

parts.note: Beds is the abbreviation for Bedfordshire, an English county
'it' as in 'that's it', exactly the thing

explanation.surface: An estate agent's pitch: humble lodgings out in the shires, just what you need.
explanation.walkthrough: BEDS is the usual short form of Bedfordshire, a county north of London.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedsit is a single rented room used for both living and sleeping, a cheap British form of lodging.

clue.text: In part of plant, allowed to distribute pamphlets

parts.note: a leaf is part of a plant
let means allowed or permitted

explanation.surface: Campaigners were permitted to hand out flyers inside the plant.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a factory, but the plant here is a growing one.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as a verb, to leaflet an area is to hand out printed sheets there, as campaigners do.

clue.text: Small organism inserting sting in rodents

indicators.note: inserting one piece in another puts the swindle inside the rodents

parts.note: mice are rodents
a sting is a swindle, so to sting is to rob

explanation.surface: A lab note about a tiny bug implanted in rodents by injection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sting' suggests an insect or a jab, but here it is slang for cheat, as in a police sting or being stung by a con man.
explanation.definitionFit: A microbe is a microscopic living thing, such as a bacterium, seen only with a microscope.

clue.text: Yahoo available on line

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another follows it

parts.note: out means available, as a library book or a new release is out

explanation.surface: Yahoo, the search site, is reachable online.
explanation.walkthrough: Yahoo looks like the internet company; it is a yahoo, Swift's brutish creature from Gulliver's Travels.
explanation.definitionFit: A yahoo is a coarse, boorish person, named after the brutes in Gulliver's Travels; a lout is the same sort.

clue.text: Female assistant upset make-up people?

indicators.note: upset letters are disturbed and rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A woman helper is upset by the people doing make-up in a dressing room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make-up' suggests cosmetics; the people make things up, so the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Fantasists are dreamers who invent stories and imagine things that are not real.

clue.text: Black and white children admitted by doctor with no capital

indicators.note: the children are let in by the surrounding pieces

parts.note: MO is medical officer, an army doctor
Rome is the Italian capital

explanation.surface: A doctor with no money takes in children, painting a bleak black-and-white picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like money, but it is a capital city; MO, medical officer, is the usual crossword doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: Monochrome means in a single colour, as black-and-white photography or film is.

clue.text: Two rings attached to European bird

indicators.note: the European abbreviation is joined on after the rings

parts.note: a hoop and an O are both rings

explanation.surface: A ringed European bird, tagged twice on the leg.
explanation.walkthrough: HOOP and O are two rings; the clue says European bird, so the definition is 'bird'.
explanation.definitionFit: The hoopoe is a crested, pinkish-brown bird with barred black and white wings, found across Europe.

clue.text: Time put into handicraft, note

indicators.note: the letter for time is placed inside the craft

parts.note: crochet is a needlework handicraft

explanation.surface: Someone spends time on needlework and makes a note of it.
explanation.walkthrough: A crotchet is the musical note Americans call a quarter note.
explanation.definitionFit: In music a crotchet is a note lasting one beat, half a minim.

clue.text: Banks are ruined in this part of US

indicators.note: ruined letters are wrecked and put together in a new order

parts.note: anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A financial crash: banks have failed in a corner of America.
explanation.definitionFit: Nebraska is a state of the Great Plains in the central United States.

clue.text: Holy word in response to ring, getting married

parts.note: 'hallo' is said on answering a ringing telephone
wed means married

explanation.surface: A sacred word spoken at a wedding when the ring is given.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ring' suggests the wedding ring; it is a phone ring, answered with HALLO.
explanation.definitionFit: Hallowed means made sacred or consecrated, as in hallowed ground.

clue.text: Don't audibly greet crewman like this on plane!

definitions.text: Don't audibly greet crewman like this on plane!

parts.note: 'hi' is a word of greeting
a jack, or jack tar, is a sailor

explanation.surface: Air-travel advice: don't shout hello to a crew member called Jack on board.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud on a plane, a cheery 'Hi, Jack!' to a sailor sounds like announcing the crime, which is why the clue says don't.
explanation.definitionFit: To hijack a plane is to seize it by force; the joke is the old warning against greeting friends named Jack at airports.

clue.text: Tries to win where some games are played

explanation.walkthrough: The sporting surface hides a romance: one word is both a suitor's verb and a playing area.
explanation.definitionFit: The word serves as a verb for wooing someone and as a plural noun for the enclosed areas used in tennis.

clue.text: Warm garment husband's not needed in Southern climate

indicators.note: something not needed is left out, so this letter is removed

parts.note: climate and weather are both the conditions of the atmosphere
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: In a hot southern climate, a husband has no need of a jumper.
explanation.walkthrough: S + WEATHER loses its H.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweater is a knitted pullover worn for warmth, a jumper in British English.

clue.text: Expose corrupt man in American bank, finally

indicators.note: the scrambled word goes inside the abbreviation
corrupt letters are spoiled, so they are rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder

indicators.note: the last letter of the word

parts.note: last letter K

explanation.surface: Uncovering a crooked employee at an American bank, at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corrupt' sounds like it describes the man, but it tells you to rearrange his letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To unmask someone is to reveal their true identity or expose their hidden wrongdoing.

clue.text: Patient man's running arrangement to reduce unemployment

parts.note: Job, the Biblical figure famed for his patience
haring means running fast, like a hare

explanation.surface: A patient man's running scheme to get people back into work.
explanation.walkthrough: The patience of Job is proverbial, from the Book of Job.
explanation.definitionFit: Job-sharing splits one full-time post between two people, spreading work among more of them.

clue.text: Old Bank of England, initially, as source of notes

indicators.note: the first letter of each of the words that come before

explanation.surface: The old Bank of England, where banknotes originally came from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'notes' suggests banknotes; they are musical notes.
explanation.definitionFit: The oboe is a woodwind instrument, so musical notes come from it.

clue.text: Vivacious spirit queen's shown in life

indicators.note: the queen's letter appears within the word for life

parts.note: bio, as in biography, means life
R is Regina, queen

explanation.surface: The queen is portrayed as lively in a biography.
explanation.walkthrough: R (Regina) goes in BIO.
explanation.definitionFit: Brio is vigour and liveliness, an Italian word familiar from music markings like con brio.

clue.text: Scoundrel promises to pay — that's odd

parts.note: a cur is a contemptible man
IOUs are written promises to pay a debt

explanation.surface: A rogue handing out IOUs: something fishy there.
explanation.definitionFit: Curious can mean strange or peculiar, as in a curious coincidence.

clue.text: Fruit taken from bed after almost one month

indicators.note: the bed comes after the shortened month
almost the whole word, so the last letter goes

parts.note: April is one month of the year
a cot is a small bed

explanation.surface: Fruit picked from a garden bed in late spring.
explanation.walkthrough: APRI (April without its last letter) is followed by COT.
explanation.definitionFit: The apricot is a small orange stone fruit related to the peach and plum.

clue.text: Silly Harry reckoned without parking in West End location

indicators.note: in the old sense of outside: the scrambled letters go round the parking letter
silly letters are foolishly jumbled

parts.note: anagram fodder
P is the map symbol for parking

explanation.surface: Silly Harry thought he could do without a parking space in central London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' seems to mean lacking, but it means outside: the anagram of HARRY RECKONED goes round P. HYDE PARK CORNER is a famous London junction.
explanation.definitionFit: Hyde Park Corner is a major road junction and landmark at the western edge of London's Mayfair, near the West End.
